output.explanation: The webhook route marked orders paid from whatever JSON was posted to it, so anyone who knew the URL could forge a PAYMENT.CAPTURE.COMPLETED event. The route now captures the raw request body through express.json's verify hook. Before touching any order, it calls a new verifyWebhookSignature helper in paypal.js, which sends the PayPal transmission headers, PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ID and the event exactly as received to POST /v1/notifications/verify-webhook-signature. The route only proceeds when verification_status is SUCCESS; a missing, forged or unverifiable delivery gets a 400 and changes nothing.

output.notes: Set PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ID to the ID of the webhook you registered for this URL in the PayPal developer dashboard, using the sandbox app in sandbox and the live app in production. Make sure that webhook is subscribed to PAYMENT.CAPTURE.COMPLETED and PAYMENT.CAPTURE.PENDING. While PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ID is unset, every webhook is rejected with 400. Mock events sent from the dashboard's Webhooks Simulator cannot be verified through verify-webhook-signature and will also get 400, so test with real sandbox checkouts instead.
